facts.text: The study varied the Mo content x in CoCrFeNiMox-Ni/MoS2-Ag-Cr2O3 composites among 0.2, 0.5, and 1.
The composites were spark-plasma-sintered under vacuum at 1250 °C and 40 MPa with a 150 °C/min heating rate and a 3 min hold.
Dry ball-on-disk tests were performed in air from room temperature to 800 °C against a 6 mm Si3N4 ball at 8 N, 0.15 m/s, and a 270 m sliding distance.
Increasing Mo caused greater FCC lattice distortion and produced increasing amounts of a hard Mo-rich tetragonal σ phase.
Dissolved Mo strengthened the matrix by impeding dislocation motion, while the σ phase suppressed plastic deformation and scratching by second-phase strengthening.
At low-to-medium temperatures, layered MoS2 provided a low-shear lubricating film and soft Ag reduced adhesion.
At 800 °C, Mo1 formed a continuous dense glaze containing NiO and the silver molybdates Ag2MoO4, Ag2Mo4O13, and Ag2Mo2O7, which separated the matrix from the counterface.
Increasing Mo from x = 0.2 to 0.5 and 1 increased composite hardness.
Hardness rose from 432 HV for Mo0.2 to 488 HV for Mo0.5 and 546 HV for Mo1.
Yield strength was nonmonotonic with Mo content, peaking at 502 MPa for Mo0.5 compared with 445 MPa for Mo0.2 and 443 MPa for Mo1.
For every composition, friction peaked near 200 °C and wear peaked near 400 °C before both declined toward 800 °C.
At 800 °C, Mo1 had a wear rate of 3.15 × 10^-6 mm3/(N·m), versus 6.6 × 10^-6 mm3/(N·m) for the Mo0.2 baseline.
